questions.q: What is the primary rule that a pattern must follow to be called a tessellation?
questions.a: The pattern must cover a flat surface completely with no gaps and no overlaps. A student who says "it just needs to be a pattern" misses the core requirement of "fitting together" perfectly.

questions.q: If you try to tile a floor with regular pentagons, you will see gaps. Why does this happen?
questions.a: Regular pentagons cannot tessellate because their interior angles do not add up to 360 degrees when they meet at a point. If a student says "because they are round," they are confusing pentagons with circles, failing to understand the relationship between interior angles and tiling.

questions.q: Can an irregular triangle always tessellate? If so, how would you prove it?
questions.a: Yes, any triangle can tessellate. You can prove it by placing two identical triangles together to form a parallelogram, which is a shape known to tile easily. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks only "perfect" or regular shapes can form patterns.

questions.q: Look at a honeycomb. Why is it a perfect example of a tessellation in nature?
questions.a: It is composed of regular hexagons that fit together without any gaps to maximize space for honey storage. A student who misses this is likely focusing on the color or material rather than the geometry of the repeating unit.

questions.q: If a shape has curved edges, like a circle, can it form a standard tessellation? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, because curved edges cannot meet to fill the space between them; they will always leave gaps. A student who thinks circles can tessellate is ignoring the "no gaps" rule of the definition.

questions.q: Design a simple tessellation on a piece of grid paper using two different colors to show the repeating unit. What happens if you rotate every second tile?
questions.a: The expected response describes how the pattern shifts or changes orientation while maintaining the "no gap" rule. A poor answer fails to acknowledge that the "no gap" rule must be preserved regardless of rotation.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A ______ is a pattern created by repeating one or more geometric shapes to cover a flat surface completely, leaving no gaps and having no overlaps.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever looked at a brick wall or a tiled floor and wondered why they look so neat and ______ fitted?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify whether a given shape can tessellate by physically arranging cut-outs or drawing them, and explain why shapes like regular pentagons fail to form a tessellation.
